subject: Request: Exec clearance for indemnity/warranty adjustment and discount — Aurelium SOW
messages:
From: Ellen Parker <ellen.parker@aurelium.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Li <marcus.li@aurelium.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Aurelium SOW v2 - warranty/indemnity question

Hi Sean / Laura,

Thanks for the revised SOW (attached). Procurement here at Aurelium reviewed the redlines and have two items they need cleared before they can execute:

1) Liability cap: they are asking Redwood to increase the total liability cap to $5,000,000 (from what I understand is your standard $1,000,000). This is a hard requirement from our legal counsel for this category of customer data.

2) Indemnity & warranty: they want Redwood to accept a broader IP indemnity (covering third-party IP claims related to the service) and to narrow your warranty disclaimer for integrations we are relying on.

In exchange, Aurelium is prepared to commit to an 18-month term and is requesting a one-time 25% credit on professional services and the first three months of subscription. We are trying to move fast and would like to sign by 2026-12-01 if possible.

Attached: Aurelium_SOW_v2.pdf (redlines) and a short risk matrix from their counsel.

Can you let me know if those two items are remotely possible and what escalation path you need? Happy to hop on a quick call.

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Parker
Head of Procurement, Aurelium Systems
ellen.parker@aurelium.com
+1 415 555 0127

Attachment: Aurelium_Risk_Table.xlsx (procurement risk summary)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Parker <ellen.parker@aurelium.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Li <marcus.li@aurelium.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aurelium SOW v2 - warranty/indemnity question

Ellen — thanks for the note and for the attachments. Appreciate the clarity on procurement's priorities. I pulled legal in and we reviewed the redlines quickly. Two quick notes:

- The liability cap change to $5M and the expanded IP indemnity are both outside our standard commercial risk thresholds and require senior authorization (exec-level sign-off).
- Legal flagged the proposed warranty language around third-party integrations as a removal of our standard protections; we can potentially accept a narrowed warranty but need contractual guardrails (e.g., notice+remedy windows, cap tied to fees, and an explicit carve-out for Redwood-hosted platform components).

To be explicit, here's what we'd need approval for from our side to move forward:
1) One-time commercial concession: 25% credit on PS + first three months of subscription (as requested).
2) Contractual risk concession: increase liability cap to $5,000,000 for this deal (non-standard).
3) Indemnity accommodation: accept customer-proposed IP indemnity limited to direct IP claims and subject to a $5M aggregate cap; Redwood legal wants to add exclusions for (a) customer data misuse, (b) open-source components we did not modify, and (c) third-party vendor modules the customer brings.
4) Contract conditions: require evidence of E&O/cyber insurance (minimum limits to be set by legal), and add a revenue-protection clause if the customer terminates early.

If you can confirm Aurelium is willing to add the insurance requirement and the limited carveouts above, I will escalate for senior authorization. Internal routing: Laura is taking legal coordination; Ben Carter (cc'ed below) will need to approve the pricing concession; Priyom Das should confirm how we will account for the one-time credit against committed ARR.

Can you confirm the insurance stance and the final committed value (so I can include accurate numbers in the ask)? If we can get that today, I'll push this to leadership for a decision.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Aurelium SOW v2 - exec authorization request (liability/indemnity)

Ben / Priyom — forwarding the thread and attachments from Aurelium. Sean summarized the concessions we would need to approve. Legal has reviewed and provided the redline with the following risk notes (summary):

- Expanded IP indemnity as written exposes Redwood to broad third-party claims without practical exclusions. Legal will accept an IP indemnity only if it is limited to direct IP infringement claims and subject to the proposed aggregate cap (see below) and the exclusions Sean listed.
- Liability cap increase to $5M is outside standard policy. Accepting it materially increases our potential exposure.
- Warranty edits proposed by the customer remove language that protects Redwood from integration issues where we don't control the third-party component. Legal wants to keep a fallback clause that retains our standard warranty for Redwood-managed components.

Commercial ask from Aurelium (per Sean / Ellen):
- 18-month committed term (revenue commitment to be confirmed by Priyom).
- One-time 25% credit on PS + first 3 months subscription.

Time pressure: procurement expects signature by 2026-12-01. We need a decision from leadership on the liability cap + approval of the commercial concession. If leadership authorizes, legal will: (a) add specific carveouts/exclusions, (b) require proof of insurance (E&O/cyber) with minimum limits, and (c) include a revenue-protection amortization schedule for the credit.

Decision requested:
- Approve or decline the $5M cap for Aurelium (one-off authorization).
- Approve or decline the 25% one-time credit (or suggest a lower %).
- Any additional controls (insurance minimum, repayment amortization, escrow, etc.).

If you want a short briefing call I can set one up; otherwise please reply with your direction.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0144

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 18:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Aurelium SOW v2 - exec authorization request (liability/indemnity)

Laura / Sean / Priyom — reviewed. I’m authorizing a one-time, customer-specific exception with the following firm conditions:

1) Liability cap: approve increase to $5,000,000 aggregate for Aurelium only. This is a one-off and must be clearly labeled in the contract as an exception with an internal expiration (no precedent).

2) Indemnity: accept a limited IP indemnity tied to direct third-party IP infringement claims only. Redwood legal will insert explicit carveouts for: (a) customer data misuse, (b) open-source components as-is, and (c) modules the customer supplies or operates. Any indemnity payments will be subject to the $5M cap.

3) Warranty: we will not accept sweeping removal of our warranty protections. Legal to preserve standard Redwood warranty for Redwood-managed components; for third-party integrations we will add a defined remedy window and an explicit customer acceptance clause for external modules.

4) Insurance & conditions: require evidence of E&O/cyber insurance with minimum limits as set by legal (provide certificate before signature). Include a revenue-protection clause that amortizes the 25% credit over the first 12 months of the committed term; credit clawback if customer terminates without cause within that period.

5) Commercial concession: approve the 25% one-time credit on PS + first three months subscription, provided legal inserts the above protections and Priyom confirms the committed ARR and that the credit will be amortized per (4).

Next steps: Laura/legal, please incorporate the exception language into the redline and route the updated SOW and contract to Ben for final sign-off after legal confirms the insurance language and Priyom confirms the committed value. Sean, coordinate with Ellen to get the insurer certificate and the final committed-value confirmation.

Ben Carter
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0101
